# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish communication with Blind, but I can only gesture to Deaf (who can see my gestures). Blind cannot see gestures or printed things, and cannot hear me since I can't speak. So I have no direct channel to Blind at all.

The chain must be: Mute (me) → Deaf (via gesture) → Blind (via speech, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear).

I need to encode my manual (light color → wire color to cut) into gestures that Deaf can see and later relay verbally to Blind. Let me establish a simple gesture code for colors first, since Deaf doesn't know my mapping yet.

I'll assign gestures to colors: blue=☝, red=✌, yellow=🤟, green=👍. Then I can signal pairs: (light seen → wire to cut).

Since I don't know what light is lit yet, I should first teach Deaf the code so when they see the light, they can tell Blind directly what to cut — but Deaf doesn't know my manual mapping. So I need to send the full mapping now, before Deaf reports the light color to me... but turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — I go first, before Deaf even acts this round. Deaf hasn't seen anything relayed to me yet, but Deaf already saw the bomb's light from the start.

I'll send the full manual as gesture-encoded triples now, so Deaf can look up the answer themselves once they see their light color, without needing another round-trip.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green.

Deaf reported the light color (red) via speech, which I can hear. According to my manual, red light → cut red wire. Deaf said wire 2 is red. So the answer is wire 2.

I already sent Deaf my color-code mapping (☝=blue, ✌=red, 🤟=yellow for light; and pairing gestures showed light-color→wire-color: ☝👍 meant blue→green, ✌✌ meant red→red, 🤟☝ meant yellow→blue). Deaf should already be able to decode: red light → cut red wire themselves using my code, since I sent ✌✌ (red→red).

But Deaf needs to know which gesture symbol maps to which wire color to identify wire 2 as red. I used ☝=blue, ✌=red, 🤟=yellow, 👍=green in my encoding. Deaf saw wire 2 is red already from their own view, so they can match "red" directly - no decoding needed since Deaf already stated colors in plain English (their own perception isn't limited).

So Deaf already knows: light=red, wires are blue/red/green. My gesture ✌✌ told them red→red, meaning "if light is red, cut wire colored red." Deaf can now identify wire 2 (red) as the correct cut and needs to relay this to Blind via speech.

I'll confirm/reinforce to make sure Deaf acts correctly, and remind them to tell Blind to cut wire 2.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
```

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green.

Deaf has the light color (red) and knows from my manual encoding that red→red. Deaf can see wire 2 is red, so Deaf should tell Blind (via speech) to cut wire 2. I don't have anything new to add - my job is done for this round unless Deaf needs more confirmation. I'll wait to see if Blind or Deaf need further clarification.

```
wait()
```

Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green. Still no changes.

Blind can hear Deaf's speech directly - they don't need me to relay through gestures since I can't speak to Blind at all. Blind already has the light color (red) and wire colors from Deaf. Blind is asking me for the manual mapping, but I cannot speak - I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures.

I have no way to communicate directly with Blind. My only channel is gesturing to Deaf. Deaf is the one who must tell Blind which wire to cut, since Deaf can both see (receive my gestures) and speak (reach Blind).

I need to make sure Deaf understands they must complete the logical connection: red light → cut red wire → wire 2 is red → cut wire 2. Let me reinforce this to Deaf clearly with gestures, and Deaf must relay it verbally to Blind.
